newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay's soybean exports rise three pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay's soybean exports rise three pct in 1996.

text.p: Paraguay's soybean exports rose three percent this year compared to 1995, the Grains and Oilseeds Export Chamber said Thursday.

Production rose 4.5 percent from 1995 to 2.4 million tonnes while exports totaled 1.6 million tonnes, according to preliminary data released by the chamber. Average yields were 2,500 kilos per hectare.
Of total exports, 42 percent went to Brazil, Paraguay's main trade partner, while 37.4 percent went to Europe and Asia.
In 1995 Paraguay exported 1.53 million tonnes of soybeans of its 2.3 million tonne harvest.
A long spell of rain in October delayed sowing of the new crop until November, and chamber experts said this could hurt estimates for next year's harvest.
Farmers aim to sow one million hectares in 1997 against 960,000 in 1996 and to harvest a record 2.5 million tonnes.
Soy production in 1994 was 1.9 million tonnes, of which 1.2 million were exported.
